answer: When a new agent identity asks to share epoch rewards, the registry requires it to post an anchor bond locked for several epochs and prove it holds a distinct hardware key. Because that stake lands before any payout, every fake identity carries real sunk cost, and letting identities whisper referrals to each other only merges them into one grove of shared, slashable collateral. A Sybil flood therefore pays the deposit times the wallet count, with no refund once a dispute confirms the duplicate.
